items.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>We develop a logic-based framework for formal specification and algorithmic verification of<jats:italic>homogeneous</jats:italic>and<jats:italic>dynamic</jats:italic>concurrent multi-agent transition systems. Homogeneity means that all agents have the same available actions at any given state and the actions have the same effects regardless of which agents perform them. The state transitions are therefore determined only by the vector of numbers of agents performing each action and are specified symbolically, by means of conditions on these numbers definable in Presburger arithmetic. The agents are divided into<jats:italic>controllable</jats:italic>(by the system supervisor/controller) and<jats:italic>uncontrollable</jats:italic>, representing the environment or adversary. Dynamicity means that the numbers of controllable and uncontrollable agents may vary throughout the system evolution, possibly at every transition. As a language for formal specification we use a suitably extended version of Alternating-time Temporal Logic, where one can specify properties of the type “a coalition of (at least)<jats:italic>n</jats:italic>controllable agents can ensure against (at most)<jats:italic>m</jats:italic>uncontrollable agents that any possible evolution of the system satisfies a given objective<jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$\gamma$$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mml:mi>γ</mml:mi></mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>″, where<jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$\gamma$$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mml:mi>γ</mml:mi></mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>is specified again as a formula of that language and each of<jats:italic>n</jats:italic>and<jats:italic>m</jats:italic>is either a fixed number or a variable that can be quantified over. We provide formal semantics to our logic<jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$${\mathcal {L}}_{\textsc {hdmas}}$$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mml:msub><mml:mi>L</mml:mi><mml:mstyle><mml:mi>H</mml:mi><mml:mi>D</mml:mi><mml:mi>M</mml:mi><mml:mi>A</mml:mi><mml:mi>S</mml:mi></mml:mstyle></mml:msub></mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>and define normal form of its formulae. We then prove that every formula in<jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$${\mathcal {L}}_{\textsc {hdmas}}$$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mml:msub><mml:mi>L</mml:mi><mml:mstyle><mml:mi>H</mml:mi><mml:mi>D</mml:mi><mml:mi>M</mml:mi><mml:mi>A</mml:mi><mml:mi>S</mml:mi></mml:mstyle></mml:msub></mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>is equivalent in the finite to one in a normal form and develop an algorithm for global model checking of formulae in normal form in finite HDMAS models, which invokes model checking truth of Presburger formulae. We establish worst case complexity estimates for the model checking algorithm and illustrate it on a running example.</jats:p>
title: Logic-based specification and verification of homogeneous dynamic multi-agent systems
